tool.name: Name MAF rows
tool.description: : species.sequence row names for pairwise MAFs, by row position
tool.command: ## Galaxy flattens newlines in <command>, so the work is a POSIX sh script with its inputs as argv, ## never Cheetah, so the same script runs as a UDT. Every input is passed in both modes: a UDT has no ## conditionals and no optional data. sh '$script' '$mode' '$input' '$species' '$renames' '$sizes' '$reference' '$output'

param.name: mode
param.label: Mode
param.help: forward: name the rows of a pairwise axtToMaf MAF. species: rename species prefixes in a multiple alignment (after roast).
param.option: forward: pairwise MAF, rows named by position

param.name: input
param.label: MAF
param.help: forward: a pairwise MAF straight from axtToMaf, bare sequence names, row 1 the reference, row 2 the query, sorted by reference position. species: any MAF whose rows are species.sequence.

param.name: species
param.label: Species line (forward; ignored in species mode)
param.help: One line, label TAB species name: the label selects this genome's rows of the renames table, the species name prefixes the query rows (79X TAB g79X).

param.name: renames
param.label: Renames table
param.help: forward: genome, hub_name, original_name with that header (hub_sequence_renames.tsv); rows whose genome is the label rename query sequences. species: from, to with that header (g79X TAB 79X).

param.name: sizes
param.label: Reference chrom.sizes (forward; ignored in species mode)
param.help: sequence TAB size for the reference genome. Every reference row must name a sequence in it, with the same size.

param.name: reference
param.label: Reference name
param.help: The reference genome's name as the rows will carry it (the hub genome name, cs10_NCBI_RefSeq_softmasked). A letter, then letters, digits or _.

validator.message: A letter, then letters, digits or _

tool.help:
**What it does**
Gives a pairwise MAF the ``species.sequence`` row names that ``roast`` (multiz) needs, and renames species afterwards.
**forward** (before roast). The input is ``axtToMaf`` output with no prefixes: every block is one ``a`` line, then row 1 = the reference and row 2 = the query, as bare sequence names::
s NC_029855.1 0 99709 + 415602 ... s 79X.00004171 316080 99682 + 442978 ...
Row 1 becomes ``<reference>.<sequence>`` and row 2 ``<species>.<hub sequence>``::
s cs10_NCBI_RefSeq_softmasked.NC_029855.1 0 99709 + 415602 ... s g79X.79X.00004171 316080 99682 + 442978 ...
The rows are told apart by **position, never by name**: a sequence name does not identify a genome (many use bare accessions, and one query genome has a sequence with the name and length of the reference's mitochondrion). Only the name is replaced; every other byte of a line is kept.
The **species line** is one line, ``label<TAB>species name``. The label selects this genome's rows of the renames table (``genome hub_name original_name``, with that header); a query sequence whose ``original_name`` is listed becomes its ``hub_name`` (``lcl|fl02_chr_009`` to ``lcl_fl02_chr_009``), others keep their name. The species name is what roast will see, so it can be an alias of the label (``79X<TAB>g79X``): it must be a letter then letters, digits or ``_``, and must not contain ``maf`` or ``eof`` (roast deletes every line that does).
The job fails, with the reason on stderr, on:
* a block with other than two ``s`` lines, or any other line inside a block; * a reference sequence missing from the reference sizes, or with a different size; * a reference row on the ``-`` strand; * a reference start that goes backwards within a sequence, or a reference sequence that starts again after another one began. multiz merges unsorted input wrongly with exit status 0.
``#`` lines outside blocks (the ``##maf`` header) and blank lines are kept as they are.
**species** (after roast). Renames the species prefix (the text before the first ``.``) of every ``s``, ``i``, ``e`` and ``q`` line, using the renames input as a two-column table ``from to`` with that header (``g79X 79X``). The reference's rows are never renamed, a new name that the rows already use is refused, and every other line is copied unchanged. The species line and sizes inputs are required by the interface and ignored in this mode.
.. note:: The interface is flat, with every input required in both modes, so that the same tool runs as a User-Defined Tool, which has no conditionals and no optional datasets.
